correction.text: Mosul and al-Jazira: Zengi atabeg of Mosul in 1127

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1139 but the infobox gives "Established: 1127", when Zengi became governor of Mosul "in charge of al-Jazeera and Northern Syria"; Aleppo followed in 1128, Hama in 1130, Homs in May 1138 (ledger).

Cliopatria's 346 k km2 for 1139-1146 (Mosul, the Jazira, Aleppo, Hama, Homs and Baalbek, taken in July 1139) also takes in Damascus, which the page gives to Nur ad-Din only in 1154 ("He captured Damascus from the Burid dynasty"; Zengi besieged it unsuccessfully in 1135, 1139-1140 and 1145). Damascus and the Hauran are removed. Edessa joins on 24 December 1144 (ledger). The Zengid page gives no area figure, so the infobox comparison is not possible. Whether Tikrit, Palmyra and Amid inside the shape were Zengid land is not on the pages opened.

363 k km2 for 1147-1151: Edessa now inside (taken 24 December 1144; the remnants west of the Euphrates in 1150); Damascus is again removed until 1154. The 1149 gain of the Antiochene east bank (ledger) lies outside this shape (gazetteer check: 0 cells at Harim) and is added by the ledger.

correction.text: Cliopatria 1152 shape without Damascus until the 1154 capture

keyframe_review.note: 385 k km2 for 1152-1168. Right for the whole once Damascus is Nur ad-Din's: "He captured Damascus" in 1154, "Syria was then unified from Edessa in the north to the Hauran in the south". Damascus is removed for 1152-1153 and enters by the 1154 gain event; The Antiochene east bank joins in 1149 (Inab), Harim is lost to Antioch in 1158 and retaken on 12 August 1164, and Banias joins in 1164 (ledger); the shape itself reaches none of these (gazetteer check: 0 cells at Harim).

correction.text: Cliopatria 1169 shape without Egypt (vassal), Libya and Transjordan: Syria and the Jazira under Nur ad-Din and Mosul

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1.16 M km2 shape for 1169-1176 stretches from Cyrenaica (18.8 E) through Egypt and Transjordan to the Euphrates and Mosul. The pages show Egypt only as "conquered in [Nur ad-Din's] name" by Shirkuh and Saladin in 1169, with Saladin swearing "nominal fealty" until Nur ad-Din's death on 15 May 1174, and say nothing of Cyrenaica or Transjordan; the Oultrejordain lordship was Christian (Kingdom of Jerusalem dossier). Egypt is therefore drawn as a vassal (ledger: the Fatimid caliphate 1169 to 17 September 1171, then Saladin's Ayyubid Egypt to 15 May 1174), Libya and Transjordan are removed, and Damascus is lost to Saladin on 27 November 1174. The pages give no area to compare.

correction.text: Cliopatria 1177 shape plus Aleppo, held by as-Salih and Imad al-Din Zengi II to 1183; valid 1177-1181, after which the ledger removes the Jazira (1182) and Aleppo (1183)

keyframe_review.note: 300 k km2 for 1177-1187 leaves out Aleppo, but the Zengids kept Aleppo until 12 June 1183 ("Imad al-Din Zengi II handed Aleppo to Saladin on 12 June"); after the spring-1176 settlement Aleppo "recognized Saladin's sovereignty" (the Ayyubid dossier may draw it as a vassal). Aleppo is added for 1177-1182 and removed by the 1183 loss. The 1177 to 1188 step (300 k to 209 k km2) is Saladin's conquest of the Jazira in 1182: "First, Edessa fell, followed by Saruj, then Raqqa, Qirqesiya and Nusaybin" and Sinjar "after a 15-day siege on 30 December" (ledger, added after review); Raqqa, Nusaybin and Sinjar are restored to Zengi II in the Aleppo exchange of 1183. Kukbary of Harran defected in 1182; Harran is not in the pages' lists and stays unsettled.

209 k km2 for 1188-1191: Mosul and the Jazira. March 1186: Saladin's "treaty left the Zengids in control of Mosul, obligated to supply military support" (an Ayyubid vassal; the Ayyubid dossier carries the tint). The shape holds Sinjar and Nusaybin (Saladin restored them with Raqqa in the 1183 exchange for Aleppo, ledger) and holds nothing at Raqqa or Edessa; the page's Sinjar list runs to 1250 while the Sinjar page puts Ayyubid control there from 1210-1220 (unsettled, see ledger 1250).

correction.text: the 1188-1191 shape continued: Mosul and the Jazira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Zengid shape for 1192-1201 but Mosul stayed Zengid (Izz al-Din Mas'ud to 1193, Nur al-Din Arslan Shah I 1193-1211 in the rulers list); the 1188 shape is carried over.

109 k km2 for 1202-1235: Mosul, Sinjar and the Kurdish hills. The Zengid line at Mosul ended in 1234 when Lu'lu' took over (rename event 1234); 1226: Lu'lu' submitted to al-Mu'azzam of Damascus after Gokbori and al-Mu'azzam attacked Mosul.

109 k km2 for 1236-1249: the emirate of Badr al-Din Lu'lu'. Lu'lu' "recognized the authority of the Mongols" after Kose Dag (1243; the page also says 1245) and acknowledged Mongol overlordship on his coinage in 1254.

109 k km2 for 1250-1259. The Zengid page: "Al-Jazira fell to An-Nasir Yusuf, the Ayyubid emir of Aleppo" in 1250 (the Sinjar line), while the Lu'lu' page has Lu'lu' holding Sinjar, Jazirat ibn Umar and Nisibin "around the year 1251": the pages disagree and the shape is kept. Lu'lu' died in 1259.

correction.text: the 1250-1259 shape continued: Mosul and its district under al-Salih Isma'il

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends in 1259 but Lu'lu's son al-Salih Isma'il ruled Mosul 1259-1262 until Hülegü "besieged the city of Mosul for nine months, and utterly destroyed it in 1262" (July 1262 on the Zengid page).

region.text: Mosul and al-Jazira

ledger.note: 1127: the Seljuks make Zengi atabeg of Mosul, in charge of al-Jazira and northern Syria. "After Aqsunqur al-Bursuqi was murdered, the Seljuks named Zengi atabeg of Mosul"; infobox "Established: 1127".

region.text: Aleppo

ledger.note: 1128: Zengi takes Aleppo from the Artuqids and unites it with Mosul. "Zengi took Aleppo from the Artuqids"; "uniting the two cities under his personal rule".

region.text: Hama, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1130: Zengi takes Hama. "He took Hama from Taj al-Mulk Buri's son, and his siege of Homs failed."

region.text: the castle of Montferrand (Ba'rin); approximate site, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1137: Zengi wins at Ba'rin and takes Montferrand from the County of Tripoli. "the permanent loss of the Crusader castle of Montferrand". The site is approximate.

region.text: Homs, held by Mu'in al-Din Unur of Damascus

ledger.note: 1138: Zengi agrees terms with Damascus (May), marries Zumurrud Khatun and receives Homs as her dowry. "received Homs as her dowry".

region.text: Baalbek, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1139: Zengi takes Baalbek after promising safe passage and not honouring it ("Zengi did not keep his word to protect his captives at Baalbek in 1139"); "The territory went to Najm al-Din Ayyub" (Saladin's father) as governor. [Reviewer me-09-c, 2026-10-25: month 7 removed: the page dates only the assassination of Shihab al-Din and the march on Damascus to July 1139, not the fall of Baalbek.]

region.text: Edessa (Urfa) and the county east of the Euphrates

ledger.note: 1144: Zengi takes Edessa on 24 December after a four-month siege. "Zengi captured it on December 24, 1144, after a siege of four months." The county's remnant west of the Euphrates lasted until 1150.

union.text: the part of the Principality of Antioch's 1152 shape that is outside its 1169 shape: the Antiochene land east of the Orontes
Harim (Harenc) and its district; coordinates 36.200N 36.517E from the Harem, Syria page

region.text: "all Antiochene territory east of the Orontes": the fortresses of Artah, Harim and 'Imm

ledger.note: 1149: after the victory at Inab (29 June) Nur ad-Din takes the Antiochene land east of the Orontes. "He did not, however, attack Antioch itself; he was content with capturing all Antiochene territory east of the Orontes" (Nur ad-Din page); the Inab page adds that he "went on to capture the fortresses of Artah, Harim, and 'Imm" and the Principality page that "Much of the eastern part of the Principality was lost". The region is the Antiochene 1152 shape minus its 1169 shape plus the Harim district (the 1169 shape still contains Harim); the Cliopatria Zengid shapes of 1147-1168 do not reach it (gazetteer check: 0 cells at Harim), so this gain adds it.

region.text: the remnants of the county west of the Euphrates

ledger.note: 1150: Nur ad-Din conquers the remnants of the County of Edessa west of the Euphrates. "He conquered the remnants of the County of Edessa west of the Euphrates"; the Nur ad-Din page has him defeating Joscelin II "for a final time" that year.

region.text: Damascus and the country south to the Hauran: "from Edessa in the north to the Hauran in the south"

ledger.note: 1154: Nur ad-Din takes Damascus from the Burids with the help of its people, unifying Syria "from Edessa in the north to the Hauran in the south". The Zengid page: "He captured Damascus from the Burid dynasty." No month on either page.
1154: Nur ad-Din makes Damascus his capital. Infobox "Damascus (1154-1174)".

region.text: Harim (Harenc) and its district; coordinates 36.200N 36.517E from the Harem, Syria page

ledger.note: 1158: Baldwin III retakes Harim for Antioch. "It was taken back by the Crusaders under Baldwin III in 1158" (Harem, Syria page); the Battle of Inab page says Harim "was not recovered until 1157". Nur ad-Din took it again on 12 August 1164.

region.text: Banias (Paneas), no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1164: Nur ad-Din "later besieged and captured Banias" after Harim; the page gives no separate date.

region.text: Harim (Harenc) and its district; coordinates 36.200N 36.517E from the Harem, Syria page

ledger.note: 1164: Nur ad-Din wins at Harim (12 August) and takes the fortress. "Nur ad-Din resumed the siege and captured Harim a few days later". Narrowed after review to Harim and its district: the rest of the Antiochene east bank was taken in 1149, and Harim itself changed hands in 1149, 1158 and 1164 (Harem, Syria page).

region.text: Fatimid Egypt, conquered in Nur ad-Din's name (Shirkuh, then Saladin as vizier)

ledger.note: 1169: Shirkuh takes Egypt in Nur ad-Din's name and Saladin succeeds him as vizier of the Fatimid caliph. "At the beginning of 1169, Shirkuh arrived and the crusaders once more were forced to retreat. This time Nur ad-Din's commander gained full control of Egypt." The Zengid page: "eventually seized control of Fatimid Egypt in 1169", "therefore bringing Egypt under formal Zengid dominion". Until 1171 the state in Egypt is still the Fatimid caliphate (the Ayyubid dossier starts in 1171). Reviewer fix: the earlier version named ayyubid-sultanate from 1169.

region.text: the Fatimid caliphate ends

ledger.note: 1171: the Fatimid caliphate is abolished on 17 September (infobox "Abolished by Saladin: 17 September 1171"); the Nur ad-Din page has "the Fatimid Caliphate was abolished in 1171". The Fatimid page itself says nothing of Zengid dominion; that is the Zengid and Nur ad-Din pages' reading.

region.text: Saladin's Egypt, the Ayyubid state founded in 1171

ledger.note: 1171: Saladin's Egypt continues as Nur ad-Din's nominal vassal after the end of the Fatimids. "Saladin continued to swear nominal fealty to Nur ad-Din until his death in 1174, but their relationship became increasingly tense" (Nur ad-Din page); "Saladin abolished the dynasty's rule and founded the Ayyubid dynasty" (Fatimid page).

region.text: Saladin's Egypt

ledger.note: 1174: Nur ad-Din dies on 15 May and Saladin's fealty ends with him. "He died at the age of 56 on 15 May 1174 in the Citadel of Damascus"; "Saladin continued to swear nominal fealty to Nur ad-Din until his death in 1174".

region.text: Damascus and the country south to the Hauran: "from Edessa in the north to the Hauran in the south"

ledger.note: 1174: Saladin takes Damascus. "Saladin arrived on 23 November and took the citadel four days later."
1174: with Damascus lost (27 November) the Zengid seat is Mosul again; infobox "Mosul (until 1234)" and "Damascus (1154-1174)".

region.text: Hama and Homs

ledger.note: 1175: Saladin takes Homs and Hama. "Saladin entered Homs and captured its citadel in March 1175"; "By mid-1175, Saladin had conquered Hama and Homs." The Zengid army was beaten at the Horns of Hama on 13 April 1175 and "retreated to Aleppo" (Zengid page). Upgraded after review from confidence 1.

region.text: Baalbek, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1175: Baalbek passes to Saladin. Bridging step at confidence 1: the Saladin page does not report Baalbek's capture (it mentions Baalbek only as Najm al-Din Ayyub's post in 1139) and the Zengid page names no town; Cliopatria's 1177 shape no longer holds it.

region.text: "half of the nearby villages" of Harenc (Harim)

ledger.note: 1177: Aleppo's as-Salih buys off Philip of Flanders and Bohemond III, who besieged Harenc in December: "As-Salih paid 50,000 dinars and renounced half of the nearby villages in favor of Bohemond." The page names no village; the 15 km circle is my reading. Mirror of the Antioch dossier's 1177 gain.

union.text: Qirqesiya (Circesium, al-Busayra); coordinates from the Circesium page

region.text: Edessa, Saruj, Raqqa, Qirqesiya and Nusaybin

ledger.note: 1182: Saladin conquers the Jazira. "First, Edessa fell, followed by Saruj, then Raqqa, Qirqesiya and Nusaybin." Neither sentence carries a year; the 1182 comes from the surrounding text and the Ayyubid dossier's gain. This is the step that takes the Cliopatria 1177 shape (300 k km2) to its 1188 shape (209 k km2); Raqqa, Nusaybin and Sinjar come back in 1183. Mirror of the Ayyubid dossier's 1182 gain. Added after review.

region.text: Sinjar, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1182: Sinjar "was taken by the Ayyubids in 1182. It fell after a 15-day siege on 30 December." The Sinjar page (read 2026-10-25) does not mention this capture and has a Zengid cadet branch at Sinjar under Zengi II from 1171.

region.text: Aleppo

ledger.note: 1183: Imad al-Din Zengi II hands Aleppo to Saladin on 12 June. "Imad al-Din Zengi II handed Aleppo to Saladin on 12 June."

region.text: Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa, restored to Imad al-Din Zengi II

ledger.note: 1183: in the exchange for Aleppo (handed over 12 June) Saladin restores Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa. "An exchange was negotiated where Zangi would hand over Aleppo to Saladin in return for the restoration of his control of Sinjar, Nusaybin, and Raqqa"; Zangi held them as Saladin's military vassals (the Ayyubid dossier carries the tint). This explains why Cliopatria's 1188 shape holds Sinjar and Nusaybin; it holds no cell at Raqqa and none at Edessa.

1234: Badr al-Din Lu'lu' ends the Zengid line at Mosul and rules in his own name; the emirate of Mosul continues. "In 1234 Lu'lu' minted the first coins in his own name"; Zengid page: the line in Mosul ended in 1234 "possibly after assassinating" Nasir ad-Din Mahmud.

region.text: Sinjar and its Jazira dependencies, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1250: the Ayyubid emir of Aleppo takes the Jazira of the last Zengid line, the Sinjar branch. "Al-Jazira fell to An-Nasir Yusuf, the Ayyubid emir of Aleppo." Disagreement: the Lu'lu' page has Lu'lu' holding Sinjar, Jazirat ibn Umar and Nisibin around 1251. Sinjar page (read 2026-10-25): a Zengid cadet branch under Zengi II (r. 1171-1197) and Qutb ad-Din Muhammad (r. 1197-1219), Sinjar "controlled by the Ayyubid ruler of the Diyar Bakr district of the Jazira, al-Ashraf Muzaffar al-Din (r. 1210-1220)" and "later ... by the ruler of Mosul, Badr al-Din Lu'lu'" (undated), which sits badly with the Zengid page's Sinjar list (Sanjar Shah 1180-1208, Mahmud 1208-1241, Mahmud al-Malik al-Zahir 1241-1250); the end date is not settled.

region.text: Mosul and its district

ledger.note: 1262: Hülegü takes Mosul in July after a nine-month siege and destroys it. "Hulagu then besieged the city of Mosul for nine months, and utterly destroyed it in 1262" (Lu'lu' page); the Zengid page gives July 1262.

region.text: the emirate of Mosul

ledger.note: 1262: the emirate of Mosul, last survivor of the Zengid state, ends with the Mongol capture. Infobox "nominal power until 1250"; Lu'lu' ruled "1234-1262" as the Luluid emirs.

notes: Zengid dynasty. Five pages opened (budget 5). Cliopatria starts in 1139 (the dynasty dates from 1127), has no shape for 1192-1201 and ends in 1259 (Mosul fell in 1262): three new keyframes. The state is treated as one: the Mosul line, the Aleppo line (Nur ad-Din, as-Salih) and the Sinjar line are branches (the page gives separate rulers lists for each); the ruler strip follows the main line. A dynasty change at Mosul in 1234 (Zengid to Badr al-Din Lu'lu', a former regent) is a rename event on the same land; the 1234-1262 emirate could instead be a state of its own (the "Luluid emirs"), a question for the reviewer. Cliopatria's 1169-1176 shape (1.16 M km2) runs from Cyrenaica to the Euphrates; the pages support only Egypt as a nominal dependency (Shirkuh and Saladin "in Nur ad-Din's name", fealty to 1174) and nothing about Libya or Transjordan, so the correction drops them and the ledger carries Egypt as a vassal; the Saladin-ruled Egypt after 1171 is the Ayyubid dossier's. Not settled: the Sinjar and Nisibin branches (the page says the Ayyubids took them in 1182 and also lists Sinjar Zengid rulers 1180-1250 and Lu'lu' holding them in 1251); the Zengid page says Jazira fell in 1250 but 1251 for the Lu'lu' page; the 1243 versus 1245 date of the Mongol submission; the Cliopatria 1177-1187 shape keeps Edessa, Raqqa and Harran that Saladin took from 1182 (the ledger now removes them in 1182; Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa return in 1183). No page gives an area figure. VASSALAGE for the suzerains' dossiers: Mosul as a vassal of Saladin from the treaty of March 1186; Mosul as a vassal of Damascus (al-Mu'azzam) from 1226; Mosul as a Mongol tributary from 1243 or 1245 (coinage 1254); Aleppo recognising Saladin in 1176; Zengid Syria nominally under the Seljuk suzerainty 1157 onwards (infobox). Counterparts needing dossiers: burid-dynasty (Damascus before 1154), artuqids (Aleppo before 1128). Gazetteer names needed: Hama, Baalbek, Banias, Sinjar, Montferrand (Ba'rin) (coordinates used for each). REPAIR 2026-10-25 (after review me-09-c). Applied: (1) the 1182 loss of the Jazira (Edessa, Saruj, Raqqa, Qirqesiya, Nusaybin; Sinjar on 30 December) and the 1183 restoration of Sinjar, Nusaybin and Raqqa; (2) the 1149 gain of the Antiochene east bank after Inab, Harim's loss in 1158 and the narrowed 1164 gain, the 1177 gain of half of Harim's villages; (3) Egypt as a vassal in two steps, the Fatimid caliphate 1169 to 17 September 1171 and Saladin's Ayyubid Egypt to 15 May 1174; (4) Hama and Homs from the Saladin page (confidence 3), Baalbek left at confidence 1 because the page does not report it. The Baalbek month fix of the reviewer was kept. Disagreement: the review asked the Fatimid and Ayyubid dossiers (me-08, me-09) to add matching events; by the schema (events.type) a vassal event is recorded by the suzerain with the vassal as counterpart, so a mirror on the vassal's side would read as the opposite relation and none is requested. Mosul as Saladin's vassal (March 1186 to c. 1202), under Damascus from 1226 and as a Mongol tributary from 1243/1245 are likewise the suzerains' events (ayyubid-sultanate /ledger/9 and /14 carry the first; the others belong to the Ayyubid and Mongol dossiers) and are not written here. Open: the end of the Sinjar line (1250 against Lu'lu' c. 1251 and Ayyubid control 1210-1220, Sinjar page); Harran in 1182; Raqqa and Edessa after 1183; Harim 1157 or 1158 (Inab page against Harem page).
